sentences.text: Also heard Mrs. Annpurna  Tiwari along with Ms. Anmol Sharma, learned counsel for  respondent No.2.

In Compliance of the Court's order dated 11.11.2024, an affidavit has been filed by Additional Chief Secretary, Forest and Climate Change, relevant paras of which are being reproduced below:-
"5. DETAILS REGARDING THE TIGER DEATH INCIDENT IN BAINKUTHPUR FOREST DIVISION AS APPEARED IN THE NEWS ARTICLE OF THE TIMES OF INDIA ARTICLE DATED 10.11.2024 5.1.

That, upon receiving information on 08.11.2024 regarding the discovery of the tiger carcass near Khankhopar Nala,
Sonhat Range in Koriya Forest Division, immediately a Preliminary Offence Report (POR) was registered.

A copy of POR dated 08.11.2024 is being attached and marked as ANNEXURE A/1.
5.2.

That, apart from the above, other immediate steps were initiated, including:
(i) Deployment of a rapid response team to secure the site.
(ii) Conducting a detailed post-mortem examination by qualified veterinarians to ascertain the cause of death (iii) Collecting forensic evidence to determine the exact cause of death.

sentences.text: That a preliminary examination of the post- mortem report has revealed that the tiger's death might have been caused by poisoning, which led to labored breathing and ultimately resulted in asphyxia.
Further, upon careful examination of Point No. 2(c) of the post mortem report, it was also observed that while all ribs were present, there was a fracture in the 10th rib on the left side.

A copy of the post-mortem report of the tiger is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/2.
5.4.

That, it is further submitted that the tiger's body was intact and the viscera and other body parts were sent for detailed histopathological and toxicological examination to the Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Izatnagar, Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, vide a letter issued by the Office of the Divisional Forest Officer (DFO), Koriya, dated 09.11.2024.

A copy of the letter dated 09.11.2024 is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/3.
5.5.

That, it is pertinent to mention that the Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Izatnagar,
Bareilly, provided a toxicological examination report vide letter dated 14.11.2024.

In the report,
samples of the lung, liver, kidney, heart, spleen, stomach, and intestinal contents were analyzed for the presence of heavy metals and commonly used insecticides.
The samples tested negative for these toxicants.
However, the results of the Histopathological Examination (HPE) are still awaited.

A copy of the toxicological examination report dated 14.11.2024 is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/4.
5.6.

That, as per the established Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for handling tiger deaths, the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) nominated Ms. Prajakta Hushangabadkar,
Officer-in-Charge and Assistant Manager, Wildlife Trust of India (WII) to ensure appropriate SOP be followed to deal with tiger mortality that happened in Sonhat, Range, Koriya Division,
Chhattisgarh vide letter dated 08.11.2024.

A copy of the nomination letter dated 08.11.2024 is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/5.
5.7.

That, after all the relevant samples were collected from the body and the post-mortem analysis was completed, the body was disposed of through incineration as per the prescribed rules in the presence of the competent authority.

A copy of the Panchanama of the incineration of the tiger's body dated 09.11.2024, is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/6.
5.8.

At this juncture, it is pertinent to mention that a senior forest officer i.e. Additional PCCF (Wildlife) visited the site of the tiger's death on 09.11.2024 and provided detailed instructions to the field officers regarding the further course of action.
He also submitted a comprehensive report on the case to the state government vide letter dated 14.11.2024.

A copy of the APCCF (Wildlife) report dated 14.11.2024 is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE -A/7.
5.9.

That, upon receiving the report dated 14.11.2024, the disciplinary action was initiated,
therefore, one Forest Guard, Mr. Pitambar Lal Rajwade, one Range Assistant, Mr. Raman Pratap Singh, and one Range Officer (Forest), Mr. Vinay Kumar Singh, were suspended.
Copies of suspension orders are annexed herewith and collectively marked as ANNEXUREA/8 (colly).

sentences.text: That, four investigation teams were constituted for field investigation by the Divisional Forest Officer (DFO), Koriya Forest Division.
The said Investigation Teams have made field investigation and submitted its daily reports.

Copies of the orders of team formation, along with their daily reports, are annexed herewith and collectively marked as ANNEXURE A/9 (colly).
5.11.

That, even Chief Wildlife Warden of Chhattisgarh also completed his field visit in the nearby areas of Gurughasidas Tiger Reserve where Tiger movements were intercepted and he took meetings of the ground staff and villagers in various villages and tried to improvise the relations and ensured them timely compensation and their safety.

5.12. That, the deponent most humbly and respectfully submits that from the aforesaid it appears that all established procedures and protocols prescribed under the relevant rules and guidelines have been meticulously adhered to in the instant case.
She further ensures that each step undertaken conforms to the prescribed legal and administrative frameworks, leaving scope for no procedural deviation.

Furthermore, appropriate corrective measures have been promptly initiated and implemented by the answering respondent to address any lapses or deficiencies identified during the course of the investigation.

At the cost of repetition, the deponent reiterates its commitment to ensure that the matter is dealt with in a manner that upholds the principles of fairness, accountability, and compliance with the rule of law to preserve the wildlife in the state of Chhattisgarh.
6. DETAILS REGARDING ELEPHANT CALF HURT BY "POTASH BOMB" IN UDANTI SITANADI TIGER RESERVE AS APPEARED IN THE NEWS ARTICLE OF TIMES OF INDIA DATED 12.11.2024 6.1.

That, the deponent most humbly submits that a news article published in The Times of India dated 12.11.2024 reported an incident involving an elephant calfinjured by a "potash bomb"
in the Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve 6.2.
That, upon receiving information about the incident, the Forest Range Officer, Mr. Shailesh Baghel, conducted an immediate investigation at the site of the incident.
All materials of forensic importance were collected from the location for detailed examination.

Pursuant to the investigation, a Preliminary Offense Report (POR) was registered as Forest Crime No. 79/19 on 09.11.2024 under relevant provisions of the Wildlife Protection Act,
1972.

A copy of the POR dated 09.11.2024 for injuring calf elephant is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/10.
6.3.

That, in connection with the aforementioned incident, the Deputy Director, Udanti Sitanadi Tiger Reserve, submitted a comprehensive report vide letter dated 12.11.2024, which provides the following details:
a) Incident Details (07.11.2024): The incident of the Satlor Range, Sitanadi.
Prima facie, it appears that the potash bomb was planted by an unidentified individual with the intent to harm or scare away the elephants.

b) Search and Tracking Efforts (08.11.2024):A Dog Squad, along with a team of veterinarians, was deployed to investigate the incident and assist in locating the injured elephant.
In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157673677/
3 c) Successful Location of Injured Elephant (10.11.2024): The injured elephant's location was successfully traced using a Thermal Drone Camera, enabling the authorities to proceed with appropriate measures for its rescue and treatment.
6.4.
That, after continuous monitoring for more than a week, it was observed that the injuries sustained by the elephant calf were healing naturally.
The calf remained in close association with its herd, and no signs of critical health deterioration were observed.
6.5. That, considering the health status of the injured elephant calf, the team of veterinarians deemed it appropriate not to capture the calf, which had already healed.
This decision was made to avoid subjecting the calf to undue stress and trauma that could arise from darting and tranquilizing.
Additionally, there was a risk that the calf might not be accepted back into its herd due to potential human imprints resulting from the capture and handling process.
6.6. That, the elephant calf is presently in good health and is moving with its herd, which is roaming the forest areas bordering the Udanti- Sitanadi Tiger Reserve.
The calf is exhibiting normal behavior, and no further complications have been reported.

A copy of the latest report from the Deputy Director, Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/11.
6.7.
That, with regard to the individual responsible for planting the potash bomb, an investigation is currently underway.
The concerned forest officials are actively working to identify and apprehend the perpetrator.
The authorities are committed to ensuring that those responsible for this unlawful act are held accountable.
6.8. That, the deponent re-affirms its commitment to the protection and conservation of wildlife.

Stringent measures are being implemented to prevent recurrence of such incidents, and all necessary steps are being taken to bring the perpetrators to justice in accordance with the law.
7.
DETAILS REGARDING THE DEATH OF A TUSKER (ELEPHANT) IN BALRAMPUR AS REPORTED IN THE TIMES OF INDIA ON 12.11.2024 7.1.

That, the deponent respectfully submits that the news item published in the Times of India dated 12.11.2024 reported the unfortunate death of a male elephant (tusker) due to electrocution within the jurisdiction of the Balrampur Forest Division.

7.2. That, upon receiving information about the incident, the Divisional Forest Officer, Balrampur,
initiated an investigation, and the following facts have been ascertained regarding the said incident:
a) That, upon receipt of the information on 11.11.2024 concerning the death of an elephant aged approximately 11 years near Murka Village in the Balrampur Forest Division, a Preliminary Offence Report (POR) was immediately registered as Criminal Case No. 18926/23 dated 11.11.2024 under Sections 9, 50, 51(1), and 52 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
A copy of the POR dated 11.11.2024 for death of elephant is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/12.

sentences.text: That, as per the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for handling cases involving the death of an elephant, the body was thoroughly examined by an expert veterinarian in the presence of Forest Officials.
The Post-Mortem Examination Report and circumstantial evidence established that the cause of death was electrocution.
A copy of the post mortem report, of the death of the elephant is annexed herewith and marked as ANNEXURE A/13.
c) That, during the night of 10.11.2024, a herd of wild elephants was observed roaming in the vicinity of Murka Village, located within the Murka Forest Beat of the Balrampur Forest Division.
Forest Officers were deployed to alert the villagers about the presence of the herd and to instruct them to refrain from disturbing the elephants.
They were also explicitly directed to ensure the removal of any illegal electrical fencing that might have been installed.

d) That, as per the investigation conducted by the Forest Department, it has been established that the death of the tusker was caused by electrocution from illegal electrical fencing installed by the accused, Mr. RambakasAyam, son of Mr. BabulalAyam.
The said fencing was unlawfully set up around farmland adjacent to the forest 7.3.

That, the illegal electrical fencing in question was reportedly connected to a high-voltage power source, which was laid out with the intent to deter wildlife, particularly elephants, from entering agricultural fields.
The installation of such fencing constitutes a grave violation of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and also endangers human and animal life.

7.4. That, in light of the findings, the Forest Department has undertaken the following actions:-
a) Immediate removal of the illegal electrical fencing in the area to prevent any further incidents.
b) Initiation of legal proceedings against the accused, Mr. RambakasAyam, for violations of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

c) Enhanced patrolling and monitoring in the area to ensure the safety of both wildlife and local communities.
d) Conducting awareness campaigns to educate the villagers about the legal consequences of illegal activities, including the installation of unauthorized electrical fences, and the importance of coexisting with wildlife.

7.5. That, the Forest Department has also recommended to the concerned electricity authority [Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Company Limited (CSPDCL)] to investigate and penalize for unauthorized or illegal connections used for electrical fencing in the instant case, in accordance with the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003 or other relevant legal statutes.

That, the Forest Department, in collaboration with the Wildlife Protection Force and the local administration, is undertaking all necessary measures to prevent the recurrence of such incidents and ensure the strict enforcement of wildlife protection laws.

sentences.text: STEPS AND ACTIONS BEING TAKEN TO PRESERVE WILDLIFE IN THE STATE OF CHHATTISGARH 8.1. Developments of Habitats for Wildlife 8.1.1.
Prey Base Development:
The forest department is consistently working to enhance the prey base inside protected areas through habitat enrichment activities, ensuring a sustainable food supply for predators.

8.1.2. Grassland Developments:
The forest department is actively engaged in creating and improving grasslands to ensure adequate fodder availability for herbivores, which constitutes a crucial part of the prey base for large carnivores.
8.1.3. Rehabilitation of Degraded Bamboo Groves:
Rehabilitation of degraded bamboo patches is prioritized to support the dietary needs of herbivorous species and maintain ecological balance within the protected areas.
8.1.4.Weed Eradication:
Systematic efforts are being undertaken to eradicate invasive species and weeds that disrupt the natural habitat, ensuring the preservation and regeneration of native flora essential for wildlife.

8.1.5. Plantation of Fruit-Bearing Tree Species:-
Large-scale plantations of fruit-bearing trees are being undertaken, particularly in areas frequented by sloth bears, to augment the food supply and mitigate human-wildlife conflicts.
8.1.6. Water and Soil Moisture Conservation Measures:
Various water conservation initiatives such as construction of percolation tanks, stop dams, and ponds are being implemented to ensure year- round availability of water for wildlife and to prevent soil degradation.
8.1.7.Sloth Bear and Leopard Conflict Mitigation:
Conflict management, particularly concerning sloth bears and leopards, is being addressed by engaging wildlife conflict management experts.

sentences.text: Dedicated forest roads are being constructed to facilitate patrolling, ensure rapid response to wildlife emergencies, and improve accessibility in remote forest areas.
b. Deployment of Tiger Trackers and Guards:
Expert tiger trackers and guards have been deployed to monitor tiger movements and maintain habitat security.
c. Training Programs for Staff and Villagers:
Training programs are being conducted for foreststaff and local villagers to build awareness about wildlife conservation, address grievances, and improve relations with the forest department.
d. Awareness Campaigns to Mitigate Human- Wildlife Conflicts:

Initiatives such as "Hamar Hathi Hamar Goth," aired across Sarguja, Bilaspur, Raigarh, and Raipur Akashwani Centers for disemminating information about the locations of Elephants in Chhattisgarh, have gained national recognition.
The people are therefore aware of the presence of the wild Elephants in advance so that they can remain alert and safeguard themselves.

e. Formulation and Implementation of Conservation Plans: Comprehensive Tiger Conservation Plans for tiger reserves and management plans for sanctuaries and national parks are formulated and executed to address conservation challenges.
f. Notification of Protected Areas:
i.

The State has notified total 3 National Parks, 11 Wildlife Sanctuaries, 1 Biosphere Reserve, and 4 Tiger Reserves, including:
Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve, Achanakmar Tiger Reserve, Indravati Tiger Reserve,
and Gurughasidas Tamor Pingla Tiger Reserve.

A copy of detailed list of notified protected areas is attached as ANNEXURE A/15.
ii.
To address the challenges posed by increasing human-elephant conflicts and to ensure the long-term conservation of elephants in the State, two dedicated Elephant Reserves have been notified.

These reserves serve as critical habitats for elephants and support their ecological and migratory needs:
a. Surguja-Jashpur Elephant Reserve:
This reserve spans across the Surguja and Jashpur districts, encompassing critical corridors used by elephants for seasonal migrations.
Conservation measures in the reserve focus on reducing restoring habitat fragmentation, traditional migratory routes, and ensuring the availability of water and forage.
b. Lemru Elephant Reserve:
Notified as a dedicated sanctuary for elephants, the Lemru Elephant Reserve is designed to minimize human-elephant conflict by providing a safe and sustainable habitat for elephants.

Efforts are underway to develop eco-friendly infrastructure, such as underpasses and overpasses, to facilitate In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157673677/

sentences.text: iii. Key Initiatives for Elephant Conservation Conflict Mitigation:

The Forest Department conducts regular community awareness programs and implements conflict mitigation strategies, including the installation of solar-powered fences and early warning systems in conflict- prone areas.

a. Rescue and Rehabilitation: Dedicated rapid response teams are deployed to address incidents of straying elephants and to ensure their safe return to forested areas.
b. Scientific Habitat Management: Ongoing efforts include the restoration of degraded habitats, creation of waterholes, and plantation of fodder species to support the nutritional needs of elephants.
C. Monitoring and Research:
Continuous monitoring of elephant populations and their movement patterns is monitored using GPS tracking and other scientific tools for informing people in advance regarding elephant location.

The notified elephant reserves, along with the proactive measures undertaken by the Forest Department, demonstrate the State's commitment to the conservation of elephants and the preservation of their natural habitats, while simultaneously addressing human- wildlife conflicts in a sustainable manner.
g. Establishment of Rescue Centers for WildAnimals:
Dedicated rescue centers for injured and displaced wildlife have been established,
including: Ramkola Elephant Rescue Center Jungle Safari Zoo Rescue Center, Raipur and Kanan Pendari Zoo Rescue Center, Bilaspur.

sentences.text: 9. ADDITIONAL INITIATIVES UNDERTAKEN BY THE FOREST DEPARTMENT FOR WILDLIFE CONSERVATION AND HABITAT PROTECTION 9.1.
Examples of Key Initiatives 9.1.1. Monitoring and Protection of Tigers in Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary:
A conservation effort has been demonstrated by the Forest Department, wherein one tiger, which settled in Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary in March 2024, has been under continuous monitoring.
Dedicated efforts have ensured the tiger's safety and well-being, leading to a significant improvement in its health.

Regular patrolling,
health monitoring, and habitat management have contributed to this success story,
which underscores the Department's commitment to tiger conservation 9.1.2.

sentences.text: As a result of persistent efforts in habitatrestoration, anti- poaching measures, and comprehensive conservation programs, the elephant population in the State of Chhattisgarh has witnessed a substantial increase.
Now the elephant population in Chhattisgarh is around 400 elephants.
9.1.3. Vaccination of Cattle to Prevent Wildlife Diseases

Recognizing the importance of controlling zoonotic diseases and viral infections that can adversely affect wildlife,
the Forest Department has undertaken systematic vaccination drives in villages located near protected areas.

a) Recent Vaccination Drive:
From October 18 to October 24, 2024, extensive vaccination efforts were carried out in villages surrounding the Udanti- Sitanadi Tiger Reserve (USTR).
b) Past Efforts:
A similar vaccination drive was conducted in the summer of 2024 in the Guru Ghasidas Tiger Reserve.
c) Ongoing Commitment:
The Department continues to ensure regular vaccination campaigns to mitigate the risks of disease transmission between domestic cattle and wildlife, thereby safeguarding the health of the ecosystem.

9.1.4. Proactive Wildlife Crime Management and Encroachment Removal in USTR The Forest Department has undertaken robust legal and enforcement measures to address wildlife crimes, illicit timber felling, and forest land encroachment, with notable achievements in the Udanti-Sitanadi Tiger Reserve (USTR):
a. Wildlife Crime Cases:
In the last two years, 29 cases related to wildlife crimes have been registered.
108 accused individuals were taken into custody and proceedings.

remanded for legal b.
Timber-Related Offenses:
In cases of illicit timber felling, 51 accused individuals have been apprehended, and the illegally felled timber has been confiscated.
c. Encroachment Removal Efforts:
In six key areas within the USTR, 276 individuals have been evicted, resulting in the recovery of 595.76 hectares of encroached forest land.
